title: 2026 Florida Gubernatorial Election
description: The 2026 Florida gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the next governor of Florida. Incumbent Republican Governor Ron DeSantis is term-limited and ineligible to seek a third consecutive term, leaving the race open. Republicans have won every gubernatorial election in Florida since 1998, and the GOP holds a substantial voter registration advantage of nearly 1.5 million voters. The Republican primary is competitive, with U.S. Representative Byron Donalds—endorsed by President Donald Trump—leading in early polls, while the Democratic primary frontrunner is former Republican-turned-Democrat Congressman David Jolly, who has selected former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate.

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
candidates.summary: Byron Donalds is a U.S. Representative for Florida's 19th Congressional District, first elected in 2020, and a leading Republican candidate for governor. He was raised in Brooklyn by a single mother and graduated from Florida State University with a degree in finance and marketing. Donalds has been endorsed by President Donald Trump and is viewed as the frontrunner in the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Jay Collins
candidates.summary: Jay Collins is the 21st Lieutenant Governor of Florida, appointed by Governor Ron DeSantis in 2025. A decorated Green Beret with 23 years of military service, he earned a Purple Heart after being wounded in combat and subsequently lost his leg but requalified as a fully deployable Special Forces soldier. Collins previously served in the Florida Senate and is running to preserve the DeSantis legacy.

candidates.name: Paul Renner
candidates.summary: Paul Renner served as the 103rd Speaker of the Florida House of Representatives from 2022 to 2024 and is a Republican candidate for governor. A U.S. Navy veteran who served in Operation Desert Storm and in Afghanistan, he is also a former prosecutor and business attorney. Renner emphasizes continuing the conservative policies advanced under Governor DeSantis and touts his record on the 'Free State of Florida' initiative.

candidates.name: James Fishback
candidates.summary: James Fishback (born c. 1995) is the CEO and founder of Azoria, a multi-asset investment firm, and a Republican candidate for governor. A fourth-generation Floridian, he is a political newcomer who has attracted attention for his anti-H-1B visa stance and a proposal to distribute DOGE-generated savings as stimulus checks. Fishback positions himself as an outsider focused on affordability and limiting data center expansion.

candidates.name: David Jolly
candidates.summary: David Jolly is a former U.S. Representative for Florida's 13th Congressional District, who served as a Republican from 2014 to 2017 and is now running for governor as a Democrat. A fifth-generation Floridian and attorney, he is the son of a minister and has been a vocal critic of Donald Trump. Jolly has selected former U.S. Representative Gwen Graham as his running mate and leads Democratic primary polling.

candidates.name: Dotie Joseph
candidates.summary: Dotie Joseph is a Democratic member of the Florida House of Representatives, representing District 108 since 2018. Born in Haiti and raised in Miami, she holds degrees from Yale University and Georgetown University Law Center. Joseph served as Minority Leader pro tempore from 2022 to 2024 and is running for governor on a platform of economic justice, criminal justice reform, and equitable access to education and healthcare.

candidates.name: Evelyn Castillo-Bach
candidates.summary: Evelyn Castillo-Bach is a Democratic candidate for governor from Pembroke Pines, Florida and a long-time registered Independent who joined the Democratic Party. She founded the Balanced Justice Network, a criminal justice reform organization inspired by her son's incarceration. Castillo-Bach campaigns on criminal justice reform, veteran support, and addressing affordability for working families.

forecast.rationale: This open-seat race begins with a favorable Republican baseline: the GOP has won every Florida gubernatorial election since 1998, and the race description notes a substantial Republican voter registration advantage of nearly 1.5 million. Candidate-level general-election polling is mixed but slightly Republican-leaning overall: one Emerson poll had Byron Donalds ahead of David Jolly by 5 points, one Cherry/Florida Chamber poll had Donalds ahead by 8, and one Change Research poll had Jolly ahead by 4. Donalds also appears to be the Republican primary frontrunner, including in the available GOP primary poll. Still, the polling is sparse, somewhat conflicting, and limited to a prospective Donalds-Jolly matchup months before the election, so uncertainty remains significant and confidence is low.
